speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether ambulances are allowed to run red traffic lights when attending to emergencies; (b) if not, whether there are plans to allow this; and (c) what are the steps that the Ministry is taking to encourage motorists to give way to ambulances.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Similar discretion is given for the drivers to make U-turns at places where it is not authorised by traffic rules.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To reduce the likelihood of an accident, SCDF has in place operating procedures.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Should an SCDF driver be issued a "Notice of Traffic Offence" for running a red light or making an unauthorised U-turn, an appeal will be lodged and Traffic Police will evaluate the case.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They will waive the offence if the driver was responding to a life-threatening emergency.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This appeal and waiver process can be avoided by providing legislative clarity that SCDF's ambulance drivers are allowed to run red lights and make unauthorised U-turns, where necessary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such exemptions already exist in foreign jurisdictions, such as California and the United Kingdom.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They should exercise civic responsibility and give way to SCDF's emergency vehicles, as this can make a real difference in saving lives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also continue to raise public awareness.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For instance, SCDF has worked with LTA to display "Give way to emergency vehicles" messages on electronic signboards located along expressways.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If there are aggravating factors, the offenders will be prosecuted in Court.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know my Parliamentary Question is asking only about ambulances, but I am wondering whether the review can also cover other emergency vehicles like the Police and fire engines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The point is if a fire engine can be there early, there might not be a need for an ambulance to come in the first place.
